145	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
146	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
147	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
148	
149	
150	def _validate_event(event: object, job_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
151	    if not isinstance(event, dict) or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
152	        raise ValueError("event must be an object with exactly job_id, "
153	                         "source_id, target_id, op and now")
154	    if event["job_id"] != job_id:
155	        raise ValueError("event job_id must match the item it is stored for")
156	    for field in ("source_id", "target_id"):
157	        if not isinstance(event[field], str) or not event[field]:
158	            raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a non-empty string")
159	    if event["op"] not in _OPS:
160	        raise ValueError("op must be commit or abort")
161	    if not _is_plain_int(event["now"]) or event["now"] < 0:
162	        raise ValueError("now must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
163	    return {field: event[field] for field in _EVENT_FIELDS}
164

166	def _validate_coord(data: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
167	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
168	        raise ValueError("coordination root must be an object with keys "
169	                         "version, key, owner, until and items")
170	
171	    version = data["version"]
172	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
173	        raise ValueError("unsupported coordination version")
174	
175	    key = data["key"]
176	    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
177	        raise ValueError("key must be a non-empty string")
178	    owner = data["owner"]
179	    if not isinstance(owner, str) or not owner:
180	        raise ValueError("owner must be a non-empty string")
181	    until = data["until"]
182	    if not _is_plain_int(until) or until < 0:
183	        raise ValueError("until must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
184	
185	    items_raw = data["items"]
186	    if not isinstance(items_raw, dict):
187	        raise ValueError("items must be an object")
188	    items: dict[str, list[Any]] = {}
189	    for job_id in sorted(items_raw):
190	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
191	            raise ValueError("item keys must be non-empty strings")
192	        pair = items_raw[job_id]
193	        if not isinstance(pair, list) or len(pair) != 2:
194	            raise ValueError("item values must be [event, error] pairs")
195	        event_raw, error = pair
196	        if error is not None and (not isinstance(error, str) or not error):
197	            raise ValueError("error must be null or a non-empty string")
198	        event = None
199	        if event_raw is not None:
200	            if error is not None:
201	                raise ValueError("event and error cannot both be set")
202	            event = _validate_event(event_raw, job_id)
203	        items[job_id] = [event, error]
204	
205	    return {"version": _VERSION, "key": key, "owner": owner, "until": until,
206	            "items": items}
207	
208	
209	def _load_coord(realpath: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
210	    # Unlike the five required inputs, the coordination file is created on
211	    # demand, so a missing file simply means the batch has never run.
212	    try:
213	        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
214	            text = handle.read()
215	    except FileNotFoundError:
216	        return None
217	
218	    try:
219	        data = strict_loads(text)
220	    except ValueError as exc:
221	        raise ValueError(
222	            f"coordination file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
223	    return _validate_coord(data)

226	def _status_of(items: dict[str, list[Any]]) -> str:
227	    # The status rules are the ones recovery_audit.get reports: pending
228	    # while any item is still [None, None], failed when nothing is
229	    # pending but at least one error is recorded, completed otherwise.
230	    if any(pair[0] is None and pair[1] is None for pair in items.values()):
231	        return "pending"
232	    if any(pair[1] is not None for pair in items.values()):

"""Coordinated batch recovery of every pending migration.

Where :mod:`carbon_market.recover` finishes one job's open ``prepare``,
this module sweeps all of them in a single coordinated batch. The batch
is described by a coordination file (``coord``): it records the
idempotency key of the batch, the owner currently holding the recovery
lease and its expiry, and one ``[event, error]`` slot per job snapped
up at creation -- ``[null, null]`` while pending, ``[event, null]`` once
recovered and ``[null, error]`` when the recovery attempt raised.

The coordination file is created on demand and guarded by a per-realpath
lock that excludes both threads of this process and other processes. A
batch with pending items may only be continued by its owner; another
owner must wait out the lease (``now`` later than ``until``) before
taking over, and whoever runs refreshes the lease to ``now + ttl``. Each
pending item is recovered through :func:`carbon_market.recover.run`
under a subkey derived from the batch key, so an item interrupted by a
crash is simply re-entered: the subkey replays whatever the interrupted
attempt already recorded in the migration journal. A batch whose items
are all resolved replays its original coordination object for the same
key; a different key is a conflict. When an already terminal
coordination file is re-entered and its history file is missing or was
left without that terminal snapshot -- a crash, or the history being
lost -- the one missing terminal snapshot is backfilled into the
history, and a replay whose terminal state is already recorded writes
nothing. Encoding, atomic synchronization and
file-error behaviour follow :func:`carbon_market.recover.run`, and a
failed write never damages the previous coordination file.

Every time the coordination object is created, taken over by a new
owner, or has one of its items settle -- the last settlement being the
batch's termination -- one snapshot ``[status, coord]`` is first
appended to a history file next to it (``coord + ".history"``). The
append -- its validation, the snapshot append, the atomic replace and
the parent-directory sync -- runs in one critical section under the
history file's own exclusive companion lock (``coord + ".history.lock"``),
held inside the coordination lock; read-only history queries take that
same lock shared and so only ever see a complete pre- or post-update
history. The status follows the rules of
:mod:`carbon_market.recovery_audit` and the coord is an
order-preserving deep copy of the object at that moment. The history
write always precedes the coordination write, so a failed snapshot
leaves the previous coordination state untouched and unadvanced; a
re-entry recomputes whatever a crashed attempt had not yet recorded and
skips the duplicate when it recomputes an already-recorded state. The
history file shares the coordination file's version, encoding and
atomic-synchronization behaviour.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import copy
import fcntl
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from typing import Any, Iterator

from . import jobs as _jobs
from . import migrate as _migrate
from . import offers as _offers
from . import recover as _recover
from .market import _load_registry
from ._jsonio import strict_loads

__all__ = ["run"]

_VERSION = 1
_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "key", "owner", "until", "items")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("job_id", "source_id", "target_id", "op", "now")
_OPS = ("commit", "abort")
_HISTORY_FIELDS = ("version", "key", "snapshots")
_STATUSES = ("pending", "failed", "completed")


class _Store:
    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
        self.realpath = realpath
        self.lock = threading.Lock()


_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}


def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _stores_lock:
        store = _stores.get(realpath)
        if store is None:
            store = _Store(realpath)
            _stores[realpath] = store
        return store


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _file_lock(realpath: str) -> Iterator[None]:
    # Cross-process mutual exclusion via a kernel exclusive lock: flock
    # serializes holders of the same lock file across processes, and the
    # kernel releases it automatically when the holding process exits --
    # even on a crash -- so a leftover lock file never blocks anyone. The
    # file itself is deliberately never unlinked: removing it while another
    # process waits on the old inode would split the lock domain. Any
    # failure to open or lock surfaces as OSError.
    lock_path = realpath + ".lock"
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _history_file_lock(
    history_realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False
) -> Iterator[None]:
    # The history file has its own companion lock (``history + ".lock"``),
    # separate from the coordination file's lock. recover_all.run holds it
    # exclusively around the whole validate/append/atomic-replace sequence
    # (directory sync included), while carbon_market.history's read-only
    # queries hold it shared only while opening and reading. A racing query
    # therefore observes either the complete pre-write history or the
    # complete post-write one, never a truncated or half-replaced file. As
    # with _file_lock the kernel releases the flock on process exit, so a
    # leftover lock file can never block anyone, and open/lock failures
    # surface unchanged as OSError.
    lock_path = history_realpath + ".lock"
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


def _validate_event(event: object, job_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(event, dict) or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("event must be an object with exactly job_id, "
                         "source_id, target_id, op and now")
    if event["job_id"] != job_id:
        raise ValueError("event job_id must match the item it is stored for")
    for field in ("source_id", "target_id"):
        if not isinstance(event[field], str) or not event[field]:
            raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a non-empty string")
    if event["op"] not in _OPS:
        raise ValueError("op must be commit or abort")
    if not _is_plain_int(event["now"]) or event["now"] < 0:
        raise ValueError("now must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
    return {field: event[field] for field in _EVENT_FIELDS}


def _validate_coord(data: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("coordination root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, key, owner, until and items")

    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported coordination version")

    key = data["key"]
    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
        raise ValueError("key must be a non-empty string")
    owner = data["owner"]
    if not isinstance(owner, str) or not owner:
        raise ValueError("owner must be a non-empty string")
    until = data["until"]
    if not _is_plain_int(until) or until < 0:
        raise ValueError("until must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    items_raw = data["items"]
    if not isinstance(items_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("items must be an object")
    items: dict[str, list[Any]] = {}
    for job_id in sorted(items_raw):
        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
            raise ValueError("item keys must be non-empty strings")
        pair = items_raw[job_id]
        if not isinstance(pair, list) or len(pair) != 2:
            raise ValueError("item values must be [event, error] pairs")
        event_raw, error = pair
        if error is not None and (not isinstance(error, str) or not error):
            raise ValueError("error must be null or a non-empty string")
        event = None
        if event_raw is not None:
            if error is not None:
                raise ValueError("event and error cannot both be set")
            event = _validate_event(event_raw, job_id)
        items[job_id] = [event, error]

    return {"version": _VERSION, "key": key, "owner": owner, "until": until,
            "items": items}


def _load_coord(realpath: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    # Unlike the five required inputs, the coordination file is created on
    # demand, so a missing file simply means the batch has never run.
    try:
        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            text = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None

    try:
        data = strict_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"coordination file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    return _validate_coord(data)


def _status_of(items: dict[str, list[Any]]) -> str:
    # The status rules are the ones recovery_audit.get reports: pending
    # while any item is still [None, None], failed when nothing is
    # pending but at least one error is recorded, completed otherwise.
    if any(pair[0] is None and pair[1] is None for pair in items.values()):
        return "pending"
    if any(pair[1] is not None for pair in items.values()):
        return "failed"
    return "completed"


def _validate_history(data: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_HISTORY_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("history root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, key and snapshots")

    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported history version")

    key = data["key"]
    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
        raise ValueError("key must be a non-empty string")

    snapshots_raw = data["snapshots"]
    if not isinstance(snapshots_raw, list):
        raise ValueError("snapshots must be an array")
    snapshots: list[list[Any]] = []
    for entry in snapshots_raw:
        if not isinstance(entry, list) or len(entry) != 2:
            raise ValueError("snapshot entries must be [status, coord] pairs")
        status, coord_raw = entry
        if status not in _STATUSES:
            raise ValueError("status must be pending, failed or completed")
        snapshots.append([status, _validate_coord(coord_raw)])

    return {"version": _VERSION, "key": key, "snapshots": snapshots}


def _load_history(realpath: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    # Like the coordination file, the history file is created on demand,
    # so a missing file simply means no snapshot has been recorded yet.
    try:
        with open(realpath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            text = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None

    try:
        data = strict_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"history file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    return _validate_history(data)


def _atomic_write(realpath: str, coord: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    text = json.dumps(coord, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"

    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".recover-all-",
                                    suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
            handle.write(text)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise

    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _ensure_snapshot(realpath: str, coord_obj: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    # Record one snapshot of the coordination object as it is about to be
    # persisted. The history is always written before the coordination
    # file itself, so a failure here leaves the previous coordination
    # state untouched and the caller must not advance it. A re-entry that
    # recomputes a state a crashed attempt already recorded -- not just
    # the immediately previous one, e.g. a missing history next to a
    # terminal coordination file -- finds it among the snapshots and
    # records no duplicate.
    #
    # Validation, the snapshot append, the atomic replace and the parent
    # directory sync all happen under one exclusive hold on the history's
    # companion lock; a shared-lock reader (carbon_market.history) can
    # therefore only ever observe the whole history from before or after
    # this update.
    history_realpath = realpath + ".history"
    with _history_file_lock(history_realpath):
        history = _load_history(history_realpath)
        snapshot = [_status_of(coord_obj["items"]),
                    copy.deepcopy(coord_obj)]
        if history is None:
            history = {"version": _VERSION, "key": coord_obj["key"],
                       "snapshots": []}
        elif history["key"] != coord_obj["key"]:
            raise ValueError("coordination key was already used with a "
                             "different recovery batch")
        if snapshot in history["snapshots"]:
            return
        history["snapshots"].append(snapshot)
        _atomic_write(history_realpath, history)


def run(
    jobs: str,
    offers: str,
    matches: str,
    reserves: str,
    state: str,
    coord: str,
    owner: str,
    key: str,
    now: int,
    ttl: int,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool]:
    """Recover every pending migration as one coordinated batch.

    Returns ``(coord, created)`` where ``coord`` is the coordination
    object itself -- keys version, key, owner, until and items, with
    items mapping each job_id (in code-point order) to its
    ``[event, error]`` outcome -- and ``created`` is ``True`` only when
    this call created the coordination file. A later call with the same
    key and no pending items replays the original object without
    renewing the lease; when the history file is missing or has not
    recorded that terminal state, the one missing terminal snapshot is
    backfilled into it, and a re-entry that finds it already recorded
    writes nothing. A different key raises ``ValueError``. While items
    are pending only the recorded owner may continue; another owner
    must wait until ``now`` is past ``until`` to take over, otherwise
    ``PermissionError`` is raised, and the lease is refreshed to
    ``now + ttl``. Creation, each takeover and each item settlement
    first append one ``[status, coord]`` snapshot to the history file
    ``coord + ".history"``; a failed snapshot leaves the previous
    coordination state unadvanced, and no path ever appends the same
    snapshot twice.
    """
    for value in (jobs, offers, matches, reserves, state, coord, owner, key):
        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
            raise ValueError("string arguments must be non-empty strings")
    if not _is_plain_int(now) or now < 0:
        raise ValueError("now must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
    if not _is_plain_int(ttl) or ttl < 1:
        raise ValueError("ttl must be a non-boolean positive integer")

    store = _get_store(coord)
    with store.lock:
        with _file_lock(store.realpath):
            jobs_real = os.path.realpath(jobs)
            offers_real = os.path.realpath(offers)
            matches_real = os.path.realpath(matches)
            reserves_real = os.path.realpath(reserves)
            state_real = os.path.realpath(state)

            job_records, _ = _load_registry(
                jobs_real, _jobs._validate_structure, "jobs registry")
            offer_records, _ = _load_registry(
                offers_real, _offers._validate_structure, "offers registry")
            match_records = _migrate._load_matches(
                matches_real, job_records, offer_records)
            _migrate._load_reserves(

            _events, lifecycle = _recover._load_state(
                state_real, job_records, offer_records, match_records)

            # Snapshot the jobs whose prepare is still open, in job_id
            # code-point order; this snapshot defines the batch at creation.
            snapshot = sorted(job_id for job_id, status in lifecycle.items()

            coord_obj = _load_coord(store.realpath)
            created = False
            if coord_obj is None:
                coord_obj = {
                    "version": _VERSION,
                    "key": key,
                    "owner": owner,
                    "until": now + ttl,
                    "items": {job_id: [None, None] for job_id in snapshot},
                }
                created = True
                _ensure_snapshot(store.realpath, coord_obj)
                _atomic_write(store.realpath, coord_obj)

                    # already recorded the history write is skipped too.
                    _ensure_snapshot(store.realpath, coord_obj)

                if coord_obj["owner"] != owner and now <= coord_obj["until"]:
                    raise PermissionError(
                        "recovery batch is owned by another owner until "
                        f"{coord_obj['until']}")
                takeover = coord_obj["owner"] != owner
                coord_obj["owner"] = owner
                coord_obj["until"] = now + ttl
                if takeover:
                    _ensure_snapshot(store.realpath, coord_obj)
                _atomic_write(store.realpath, coord_obj)

                    continue

                        jobs, offers, matches, reserves, state,
                        job_id, subkey, now)
                    pair[0] = event
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - record and continue
                    pair[1] = type(exc).__name__
                _ensure_snapshot(store.realpath, coord_obj)
                _atomic_write(store.realpath, coord_obj)

1	"""Persistent cross-job migration batches.
2	
3	The single-job layers already cover one booking end to end -- the trade,
4	dispatch, a launch plan, a migration advice with its reservation, claim,
5	receipts, recovery and a terminal settlement fixing the job's current
6	binding -- but nothing coordinates those steps across jobs. This module
7	adds the coordination: one persistent migration batch takes one complete
8	snapshot of the nine business ledgers, fixes its members, drives each
9	member's ``keep``/``migrate`` round with optional per-job receipts,
10	survives a crash mid-batch and settles every terminal migration before
11	the batch closes.
12	
13	:func:`run` is the only write entry point. The first call for a batch
14	key fixes the members forever: every accepted job that already holds a
15	trade and is not driven by another still-open batch, ordered by job id.
16	The judgment is rooted at the latest completed binding
17	``rebalance.current`` returns (the immutable trade when there is none):
18	
19	* a job with no current-round migration evidence whose booking is
20	  finished or in flight through the baseline layers simply stays on its
21	  current binding (``keep``);
22	* otherwise a fresh advice is evaluated at the batch moment; a ``keep``
23	  advice completes directly and a ``migrate`` advice is reserved and
24	  claimed under stable request keys;
25	* an unclaimed reservation rooted at the current binding is claimed;
26	* an active plan receives the receipt that names its next pending step,
27	  waits while the plan lease is valid without such a receipt, and is
28	  recovered once the lease has strictly expired;
29	* a ``migrated``, ``failed`` or ``interrupted`` plan rooted at the
30	  current binding enters settlement.
31	
32	Every downstream action (``evaluate``, ``apply``, ``start``, ``record``,
33	``recover``, ``settle``) and its full parameters are persisted under a
34	stable request key *before* the existing interface is called, and the
35	item only advances after success, so a crashed call replays the very
36	same request and a completed phase is never redone; a persisted request
37	always belongs to the generation it rooted and receipts, recovery and
38	settlement name that plan explicitly, never a later generation. One
39	member's business exception saves the public exception class and fails
40	just that member, while the other members continue.
41	
42	An active batch may only be continued by its current owner; another
43	owner may take over only after the coordination lease has strictly
44	expired. The coordination ledger (version 1, sections ``version``,
45	``batches`` and an append-only ``audit``) is one compact UTF-8 JSON
46	document with non-ASCII written through, decimal integers and exactly
47	one trailing newline.
48	"""
49	
50	from __future__ import annotations
51	
52	import contextlib
53	import copy
54	import fcntl
55	import json
56	import os
57	import tempfile
58	import threading
59	from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator
60	
61	from . import rebalance as _rebalance
62	from ._jsonio import finite_loads
63	
64	__all__ = ["run", "get"]
65	
66	_VERSION = 1
67	_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "batches", "audit")
68	_BATCH_FIELDS = ("key", "owner", "until", "status", "inputs", "items")
69	_ITEM_FIELDS = ("job_id", "plan_key", "phase", "request_key", "lease",
70	                "error", "snapshot")
71	_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "at", "batch")
72	# Field order of the recorded input map; the values are resolved real
73	# paths, so one batch permanently names one exact business ledger set.
74	_INPUT_NAMES = ("advice", "dispatch", "execution", "jobs", "ledger",
75	                "settlements", "signals", "supply", "trades")
76	_BATCH_STATUSES = ("pending", "completed")
77	# Coarse item stage. evaluating/reserved/claimed persist the next pending
78	# downstream call as a marker snapshot; active drives a claimed plan with
79	# receipts, waiting or recovery; settling persists the settlement call;
80	# kept/settled/failed are terminal.
81	_ITEM_PHASES = ("kept", "evaluating", "reserved", "claimed", "active",
82	                "settling", "settled", "failed")
83	_ITEM_TERMINAL = ("kept", "settled", "failed")
84	_MARKER_ACTIONS = ("evaluate", "apply", "start", "record", "recover",
85	                   "settle")
86	_PLAN_TERMINAL = ("migrated", "failed", "interrupted")
87	_STEPS = ("copy", "switch")
88	_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"
89	_PREFIX = ".migration-batch-"

92	class _Store:
93	    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
94	        self.realpath = realpath
95	        self.lock = threading.Lock()
96	
97	
98	_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
99	_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}
100	
101	
102	def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
103	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
104	    with _stores_lock:
105	        store = _stores.get(realpath)
106	        if store is None:
107	            store = _Store(realpath)

112	def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
113	    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
114	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
115

117	@contextlib.contextmanager
118	def _lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
119	    # As in the other ledgers, the companion lock file is never unlinked
120	    # and an flock is released by the kernel on process exit, so equal
121	    # real paths share one lock across threads and processes.
122	    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
123	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
124	    try:
125	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
126	        try:
127	            yield
128	        finally:
129	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
130	    finally:
131	        os.close(fd)

135	    keys = list(mapping)
136	    if keys != sorted(keys):
137	        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")

141	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
142	    try:
143	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
144	    finally:
145	        os.close(dir_fd)

148	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str, old_bytes: bytes | None,
149	                   first: BaseException) -> None:
150	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held,
151	    # or remove a ledger that did not exist beforehand, then sync the
152	    # directory. A failed recovery chains after the original error.
153	    try:
154	        if old_bytes is None:
155	            try:
156	                os.unlink(realpath)
157	            except FileNotFoundError:
158	                pass
159	        else:
160	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
161	                dir=directory, prefix=_PREFIX + "restore-", suffix=".tmp")
162	            try:
163	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
164	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
165	                    handle.flush()
166	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
167	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
168	            except BaseException:
169	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
170	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
171	                raise
172	        _fsync_directory(directory)
173	    except OSError as recovery:
174	        raise recovery from first
175	
176	
177	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
178	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
179	    # One durable commit through a synced same-directory temporary file,
180	    # an atomic replace and a directory fsync, restoring the pre-call
181	    # bytes (and clearing the leftover fragment) on any failure.
182	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
183	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
184	        dir=directory, prefix=_PREFIX, suffix=".tmp")
185	    try:
186	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
187	            handle.write(payload)
188	            handle.flush()
189	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
190	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
191	    except BaseException:
192	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
193	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
194	        raise
195	    try:
196	        _fsync_directory(directory)
197	    except BaseException as first:
198	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
199	        raise
200	
201	
202	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
203	# Stable request keys
204	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
205	
206	
207	def _stable_key(batch_key: str, job_id: str, tag: str) -> str:
208	    # Stable from the batch key, the member and the phase; the length
209	    # prefix makes the join unambiguous. Every downstream request is
210	    # replayed under exactly this key, so a crashed call never starts a
211	    # second evaluate, reservation, claim, receipt, recovery or
212	    # settlement.
213	    return f"{len(batch_key)}:{batch_key}{job_id}\t{tag}"
214	
215	
216	def _plan_key_for(batch_key: str, job_id: str) -> str:
217	    # The migration plan's own start key for a plan this batch begins;
218	    # it binds every later receipt, recovery and settlement to this one
219	    # generation so a pending request can never cross into a later plan.
220	    return _stable_key(batch_key, job_id, "start")
221	
222	
223	def _settle_key_for(plan_key: str) -> str:
224	    # The settlement key derives from the plan's start key alone, so a
225	    # crash between settle's pending and final writes is replayed under
226	    # the same key even by a later batch that picks the plan up.
227	    return f"{len(plan_key)}:settle\t{plan_key}"
228	
229	
230	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
231	# Snapshot over the nine business ledgers
232	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
233	
234	
235	class _Snapshot:
236	    """One validated read of the nine business ledgers."""
237	
238	    def __init__(self, reals: dict[str, str]) -> None:
239	        self.reals = reals
240	        # The seven baseline layers are read exactly as
241	        # rebalance._load_snapshot_layers does, except that a missing
242	        # advice ledger is an empty one: the first member that judges a
243	        # round creates it through rebalance.evaluate.
244	        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = \
245	            _rebalance._jobs._load_submit_file(reals["jobs"])
246	        if job_raw is None:
247	            raise FileNotFoundError(
248	                f"acceptance file {reals['jobs']!r} does not exist")
249	        if job_raw != _rebalance._jobs._serialize_submit_file(
250	                accepted, _job_map, _job_events):
251	            raise ValueError(
252	                f"acceptance file {reals['jobs']!r} is not in canonical "
253	                "compact form")
254	        history, _supply_map, _supply_events, supply_raw = \
255	            _rebalance._resources._load_file(reals["supply"])
256	        if supply_raw is None:
257	            raise FileNotFoundError(
258	                f"supply file {reals['supply']!r} does not exist")
259	        signal_history, _signal_map, _signal_events, signal_raw = \
260	            _rebalance._signals._load_file(reals["signals"])
261	        if signal_raw is None:
262	            raise FileNotFoundError(
263	                f"signal file {reals['signals']!r} does not exist")
264	        cleared, _clear_keys, trades_raw = _rebalance._market.\
265	            _load_clear_ledger(
266	                reals["trades"], accepted, history, signal_history)
267	        if trades_raw is None:
268	            raise FileNotFoundError(
269	                f"clearing ledger {reals['trades']!r} does not exist")
270	        decisions, _dispatch_keys, _dispatch_events, dispatch_raw = \
271	            _rebalance._dispatch._load_ledger(reals["dispatch"])
272	        if dispatch_raw is None:
273	            raise FileNotFoundError(
274	                f"dispatch ledger {reals['dispatch']!r} does not exist")
275	        self.exec_plans, _plan_keys, _plan_events = \
276	            _rebalance._execution._load_existing_ledger(
277	                reals["execution"])[:3]
278	        advice_records, _advice_events, _advice_raw = \
279	            _rebalance._load_ledger(
280	                reals["advice"], accepted, cleared, history,
281	                signal_history, defer_current=True)
282	        self.accepted = accepted
283	        self.history = history
284	        self.signal_history = signal_history
285	        self.cleared = cleared
286	        self.decisions = decisions
287	        self.advice_records = advice_records
288	        intents, plans, idempotency, events, version, intent_raw = \
289	            _rebalance._load_intent_ledger(
290	                reals["ledger"], self.accepted, self.cleared, self.history,
291	                self.signal_history, self.advice_records)
292	        if intent_raw is not None \
293	                and version != _rebalance._INTENT_VERSION_V3:
294	            # Only the history layout keeps every generation apart; a
295	            # legacy ledger is upgraded in memory for reading and is
296	            # never rewritten by this module. A missing ledger is simply
297	            # empty: the first downstream apply creates it.
298	            intents, plans, idempotency, events = \
299	                _rebalance._upgrade_intent_ledger_v3(
300	                    intents, plans, idempotency, events)
301	        self.intents = intents
302	        self.plans = plans
303	        self.idempotency = idempotency
304	        self.events = events
305	        records, settle_bindings, _events, _settle_raw = _rebalance.\
306	            _load_settlement_ledger(
307	                reals["settlements"], self.accepted, self.cleared, plans,
308	                idempotency, events, _rebalance._INTENT_VERSION_V3)
309	        # A missing settlement ledger is simply empty: the first member
310	        # that reaches settlement creates it through rebalance.settle.
311	        self.settlements = records
312	        self.settle_bindings = settle_bindings
313	        self.completed, self.pending_jobs = \
314	            _rebalance._lineage_from_settlement_records(records)
315	        for advice_record in self.advice_records.values():
316	            _rebalance._ground_advice_current(
317	                advice_record, self.cleared,
318	                _rebalance._settlement_currents(self.completed))

322	        return {name: self.reals[name] for name in _INPUT_NAMES}

328	    def current_binding(self, job_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
329	        # The judgment source is current: the latest completed binding
330	        # or the immutable trade's frozen version as generation 0.
331	        latest = _rebalance._latest_completed_binding(
332	            self.completed, job_id)
333	        if latest is not None:
334	            return copy.deepcopy(latest["after"])
335	        trade = self.cleared[job_id]
336	        return {"resource_id": trade["resource_id"],
337	                "version": trade["version"]}

339	    def rooted_plans(self, job_id: str,
340	                     binding: dict[str, Any]) -> list[tuple[str,
341	                                                            dict[str, Any]]]:
342	        return sorted(((start_key, plan) for start_key, plan
343	                       in self.plans.items()
344	                       if plan["job_id"] == job_id
345	                       and plan["source"] == binding),
346	                      key=lambda entry: (entry[1]["at"], entry[0]))
347	
348	    def unclaimed_rooted_intent(
349	        self, job_id: str, binding: dict[str, Any],
350	    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
351	        # The newest reservation rooted at the current binding that no
352	        # start request has claimed yet.
353	        claimed = _rebalance._claimed_intent_refs(
354	            self.plans, self.idempotency, _rebalance._INTENT_VERSION_V3)
355	        candidates = [(ref, intent) for ref, intent in self.intents.items()
356	                      if ref not in claimed and intent["job_id"] == job_id
357	                      and intent["source"] == binding]
358	        if not candidates:
359	            return None
360	        return max(candidates, key=lambda entry: (entry[1]["at"], entry[0]))
361	
362	    def terminal_moment(self, plan: dict[str, Any],
363	                        plan_key: str) -> int:
364	        return _rebalance._terminal_plan_at(
365	            plan, self.events, plan_key, _rebalance._INTENT_VERSION_V3)

367	    def settle_request(
368	        self, job_id: str, plan_key: str, at: int, fallback_key: str,
369	    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
370	        # When a previous crashed run already bound a settlement request
371	        # to this terminal plan, re-entry (even from a later batch)
372	        # replays that same key and moment; otherwise the caller's
373	        # stable key is used for the first settlement.
374	        for existing_key, request in self.settle_bindings.items():
375	            if request["job_id"] == job_id \
376	                    and request["plan_key"] == plan_key:
377	                return existing_key, request["at"]
378	        return fallback_key, at

386	_MARKER_REQUEST_FIELDS = {
387	    "evaluate": ("at",),
388	    "apply": ("advice_key", "at"),
389	    "start": ("owner", "lease_end", "at"),
390	    "record": ("owner", "step", "result", "receipt", "at"),
391	    "recover": ("owner", "at"),
392	    "settle": ("plan_key", "at"),
393	}

395	
396	def _marker(action: str, **params: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
397	    # Persisted before the downstream interface is called: the action
398	    # name and the exact parameters the crash re-entry must replay.
399	    return {"action": action,
400	            "request": {field: params[field]
401	                        for field in _MARKER_REQUEST_FIELDS[action]}}
402	
403	
404	def _is_marker(value: object) -> bool:
405	    return isinstance(value, dict) \
406	        and set(value.keys()) == {"action", "request"} \
407	        and isinstance(value.get("action"), str) \
408	        and isinstance(value.get("request"), dict)
409	
410	
411	def _validate_marker(raw: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
412	    if not _is_marker(raw):
413	        raise ValueError("migration batch item snapshot must be a result "
414	                         "record or a pending-action marker")
415	    action = raw["action"]  # type: ignore[index]
416	    if action not in _MARKER_ACTIONS:
417	        raise ValueError("migration batch marker action is invalid")
418	    request = raw["request"]  # type: ignore[index]
419	    fields = _MARKER_REQUEST_FIELDS[action]
420	    if set(request.keys()) != set(fields):
421	        raise ValueError("migration batch marker request has invalid "
422	                         "fields")
423	    for field in ("owner", "advice_key", "receipt", "step", "plan_key"):
424	        if field in request and (not isinstance(request[field], str)
425	                                 or not request[field]):
426	            raise ValueError(f"marker request {field} must be a non-empty "
427	                             "string")
428	    if "step" in request and request["step"] not in _STEPS:
429	        raise ValueError("marker step must be copy or switch")
430	    if "result" in request \
431	            and request["result"] not in ("succeeded", "failed"):
432	        raise ValueError("marker result must be succeeded or failed")
433	    for field, minimum in (("at", 0), ("lease_end", 1)):
434	        if field in request:
435	            value = request[field]
436	            if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < minimum:
437	                raise ValueError(f"marker {field} is invalid")
438	    return {"action": action, "request": dict(request)}

446	def _validate_inputs(raw: object) -> dict[str, str]:
447	    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw.keys()) != set(_INPUT_NAMES):
448	        raise ValueError("batch inputs must name the nine business "
449	                         "ledgers")
450	    paths: dict[str, str] = {}
451	    for name in _INPUT_NAMES:
452	        value = raw[name]
453	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
454	            raise ValueError("batch input paths must be non-empty "
455	                             "strings")
456	        paths[name] = value
457	    if len(set(paths.values())) != 9:
458	        raise ValueError("batch input paths must be distinct")
459	    return paths

462	def _validate_item(
463	    raw: object,
464	    job_id: object,
465	    snapshot: _Snapshot,
466	) -> dict[str, Any]:
467	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
468	        raise ValueError("batch item keys must be non-empty strings")
469	    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw.keys()) != set(_ITEM_FIELDS):
470	        raise ValueError("migration batch item has invalid fields")
471	    if raw["job_id"] != job_id:
472	        raise ValueError("migration batch item key must match its job id")
473	    plan_key = raw["plan_key"]
474	    if plan_key is not None and (not isinstance(plan_key, str)
475	                                 or not plan_key):
476	        raise ValueError("migration batch item plan_key must be null or a "
477	                         "non-empty string")
478	    phase = raw["phase"]
479	    if phase not in _ITEM_PHASES:
480	        raise ValueError("migration batch item phase is invalid")
481	    request_key = raw["request_key"]
482	    if not isinstance(request_key, str) or not request_key:
483	        raise ValueError("migration batch item request_key must be a "
484	                         "non-empty string")
485	    lease = raw["lease"]
486	    if lease is not None and (not _is_plain_int(lease) or lease < 1):
487	        raise ValueError("migration batch item lease must be null or a "
488	                         "positive integer")
489	    error = raw["error"]
490	    if error is not None and (not isinstance(error, str) or not error):
491	        raise ValueError("migration batch item error must be null or a "
492	                         "non-empty string")
493	    item_snapshot = raw["snapshot"]
494	
495	    if job_id not in snapshot.accepted:
496	        raise ValueError("migration batch item must reference an accepted "
497	                         "job")
498	    if snapshot.cleared.get(job_id) is None:
499	        raise ValueError("migration batch item must reference a recorded "
500	                         "trade")
501	    binding_choices = [{"resource_id": snapshot.cleared[job_id]["resource_id"],
502	                        "version": snapshot.cleared[job_id]["version"]}]
503	    binding_choices.extend(record["after"] for record
504	                          in snapshot.completed.get(job_id, ()))
505	
506	    if phase == "kept":
507	        if plan_key is not None or lease is not None or error is not None:
508	            raise ValueError("a kept item must not carry plan, lease or "
509	                             "error data")
510	        if item_snapshot not in binding_choices:
511	            raise ValueError("a kept item snapshot must be a current "
512	                             "binding")
513	    elif phase == "failed":
514	        if error is None:
515	            raise ValueError("a failed item must carry the public error "
516	                             "class name")
517	        if item_snapshot is not None:
518	            raise ValueError("a failed item must not carry a snapshot")
519	    else:
520	        if plan_key is None or error is not None:
521	            raise ValueError("an active migration item must name its "
522	                             "plan key and carry no error")
523	        if _is_marker(item_snapshot):
524	            marker = _validate_marker(item_snapshot)
525	            action = marker["action"]
526	            # The persisted action must match the stage that waits on
527	            # it; a mismatched marker is a broken reference just like a
528	            # missing plan or advice record.
529	            expected_actions = {
530	                "evaluating": ("evaluate",),
531	                "reserved": ("apply",),
532	                "claimed": ("start",),
533	                "active": ("record", "recover"),
534	                "settling": ("settle",),
535	            }[phase]
536	            if action not in expected_actions:
537	                raise ValueError("migration batch item marker action does "
538	                                 "not match its phase")
539	            if action == "apply":
540	                advice = snapshot.advice_records.get(
541	                    marker["request"]["advice_key"])
542	                if advice is None or advice["job_id"] != job_id \
543	                        or advice["recommendation"] != "migrate":
544	                    raise ValueError("apply marker must reference a "
545	                                     "recorded migrate advice for the job")
546	            elif action == "start":
547	                if lease != marker["request"]["lease_end"]:
548	                    raise ValueError("start marker lease must match the "
549	                                     "item lease")
550	            elif action in ("record", "recover"):
551	                plan = snapshot.plans.get(plan_key)
552	                if plan is None or plan["job_id"] != job_id:
553	                    raise ValueError("record/recover marker must reference "
554	                                     "a recorded migration plan")
555	            elif action == "settle":
556	                if marker["request"]["plan_key"] != plan_key:
557	                    raise ValueError("settle marker must name the item's "
558	                                     "plan")
559	                settled_already = any(
560	                    record["job_id"] == job_id
561	                    and record["plan_key"] == plan_key
562	                    for record in snapshot.settlements.values())
563	                plan = snapshot.plans.get(plan_key)
564	                if not settled_already and (
565	                        plan is None or plan["job_id"] != job_id
566	                        or plan["state"] not in _PLAN_TERMINAL):
567	                    raise ValueError("settle marker must reference a "
568	                                     "terminal migration plan")
569	        elif phase == "settled":
570	            settled = next((record for record in snapshot.settlements.values()
571	                            if record["job_id"] == job_id
572	                            and record["plan_key"] == plan_key), None)
573	            if settled is None or item_snapshot != settled:
574	                raise ValueError("a settled item must snapshot its "
575	                                 "settlement record")
576	        else:
577	            if phase != "active":
578	                raise ValueError(f"a {phase} item must carry a pending-"
579	                                 "action marker")
580	            plan = snapshot.plans.get(plan_key)
581	            if plan is None or plan["job_id"] != job_id:
582	                raise ValueError("migration batch item must reference a "
583	                                 "recorded migration plan")
584	            if item_snapshot != plan:
585	                raise ValueError("migration batch item snapshot must be "
586	                                 "the current plan or a pending marker")
587	            if lease != plan["lease_end"]:
588	                raise ValueError("migration batch item lease must be the "
589	                                 "plan lease end")
590	
591	    return {
592	        "job_id": job_id,
593	        "plan_key": plan_key,
594	        "phase": phase,
595	        "request_key": request_key,
596	        "lease": lease,
597	        "error": error,
598	        "snapshot": copy.deepcopy(item_snapshot),
599	    }

602	def _validate_ledger(
603	    data: object,
604	    snapshots: dict[frozenset[tuple[str, str]], _Snapshot],
605	    default_inputs: dict[str, str] | None,
606	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]],
607	           dict[str, str]]:
608	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
609	        raise ValueError("migration coordination ledger root must be an "
610	                         "object with keys version, batches and audit")
611	    if not _is_plain_int(data["version"]) or data["version"] != _VERSION:
612	        raise ValueError("unsupported migration coordination ledger "
613	                         "version")
614	    batches_raw = data["batches"]
615	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
616	    if not isinstance(batches_raw, dict) or not isinstance(audit_raw, list):
617	        raise ValueError("batches must be an object and audit a list")
618	    _check_sorted_keys(batches_raw, "batches")
619	
620	    batches: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
621	    completed: set[str] = set()
622	    ledger_inputs: dict[str, str] | None = None
623	    for batch_key, batch_raw in batches_raw.items():
624	        if not isinstance(batch_key, str) or not batch_key:
625	            raise ValueError("batch keys must be non-empty strings")
626	        if not isinstance(batch_raw, dict) \
627	                or set(batch_raw.keys()) != set(_BATCH_FIELDS):
628	            raise ValueError("migration batch has invalid fields")
629	        if batch_raw["key"] != batch_key:
630	            raise ValueError("batch key does not match its map key")
631	        owner = batch_raw["owner"]
632	        if not isinstance(owner, str) or not owner:
633	            raise ValueError("batch owner must be a non-empty string")
634	        until = batch_raw["until"]
635	        if not _is_plain_int(until) or until < 1:
636	            raise ValueError("batch until must be a positive integer")
637	        status = batch_raw["status"]
638	        if status not in _BATCH_STATUSES:
639	            raise ValueError("batch status is invalid")
640	        inputs = _validate_inputs(batch_raw["inputs"])
641	        if ledger_inputs is None:
642	            ledger_inputs = inputs
643	        elif inputs != ledger_inputs:
644	            raise ValueError("batches in one coordination ledger must "
645	                             "share one business ledger set")
646	        items_raw = batch_raw["items"]
647	        if not isinstance(items_raw, dict):
648	            raise ValueError("batch items must be an object")
649	        _check_sorted_keys(items_raw, "batch items")
650	
651	        snapshot = snapshots.get(frozenset(inputs.items()))
652	        if snapshot is None:
653	            raise ValueError("batch inputs do not name the loaded "
654	                             "business snapshot")
655	        items: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
656	        for member_key, item_raw in items_raw.items():
657	            item = _validate_item(item_raw, member_key, snapshot)
658	            items[member_key] = item
659	        if status == "completed":
660	            if any(item["phase"] not in _ITEM_TERMINAL
661	                   for item in items.values()):
662	                raise ValueError("a completed batch may not hold active "
663	                                 "items")
664	            completed.add(batch_key)
665	        batches[batch_key] = {
666	            "key": batch_key,
667	            "owner": owner,
668	            "until": until,
669	            "status": status,
670	            "inputs": inputs,
671	            "items": items,
672	        }
673	
674	    audit: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
675	    seen_events: set[str] = set()
676	    last_key = ""
677	    for event_raw in audit_raw:
678	        if not isinstance(event_raw, dict) \
679	                or set(event_raw.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
680	            raise ValueError("migration audit event has invalid fields")
681	        event_key = event_raw["key"]
682	        if not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
683	            raise ValueError("migration audit event key must be a "
684	                             "non-empty string")
685	        if event_key <= last_key:
686	            # The audit is append-only: out-of-order or duplicated events
687	            # are both illegal.
688	            raise ValueError("migration audit must be strictly ordered "
689	                             "and unique")
690	        last_key = event_key
691	        if event_key in seen_events:
692	            raise ValueError("migration audit keys must be unique")
693	        seen_events.add(event_key)
694	        at = event_raw["at"]
695	        if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
696	            raise ValueError("migration audit moment must be a non-"
697	                             "boolean non-negative integer")
698	        batch = batches.get(event_key)
699	        if batch is None or batch["status"] != "completed":
700	            raise ValueError("migration audit event must reference a "
701	                             "completed batch")
702	        if event_raw["batch"] != batch:
703	            raise ValueError("migration audit event batch does not match "
704	                             "its batch")
705	        audit.append({"key": event_key, "at": at,
706	                      "batch": copy.deepcopy(batch)})
707	
708	    # Exactly one closing event per completed batch, none for a batch
709	    # still running.
710	    if seen_events != completed:
711	        raise ValueError("migration audit events must match the completed "
712	                         "batches")
713	    if ledger_inputs is None:
714	        if default_inputs is None:
715	            raise ValueError("a migration coordination ledger must hold "
716	                             "at least one batch")
717	        ledger_inputs = default_inputs
718	    return batches, audit, ledger_inputs
719

721	def _canonical_item(item: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
722	    return {field: copy.deepcopy(item[field]) for field in _ITEM_FIELDS}

725	def _canonical_batch(batch: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
726	    return {
727	        "key": batch["key"],
728	        "owner": batch["owner"],
729	        "until": batch["until"],
730	        "status": batch["status"],
731	        "inputs": {name: batch["inputs"][name] for name in _INPUT_NAMES},
732	        "items": {job_id: _canonical_item(batch["items"][job_id])
733	                  for job_id in sorted(batch["items"])},
734	    }

737	def _canonical_bytes(
738	    batches: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
739	    audit: list[dict[str, Any]],
740	) -> bytes:
741	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, sections in their
742	    # fixed field order, batches and their items code-point sorted and
743	    # the audit appended in strict key order, terminated by exactly one
744	    # newline.
745	    payload = {
746	        "version": _VERSION,
747	        "batches": {key: _canonical_batch(batches[key])
748	                    for key in sorted(batches)},
749	        "audit": [{"key": event["key"], "at": event["at"],
750	                   "batch": _canonical_batch(event["batch"])}
751	                  for event in sorted(audit, key=lambda event: event["key"])],
752	    }
753	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
754	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
755	    return text.encode("utf-8")

758	def _load_coordination(
759	    realpath: str,
760	    snapshots: dict[frozenset[tuple[str, str]], _Snapshot],
761	    default_inputs: dict[str, str] | None = None,
762	) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]],
763	           dict[str, str], bytes | None]:
764	    try:
765	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
766	            raw = handle.read()
767	    except FileNotFoundError:
768	        if default_inputs is None:
769	            raise
770	        return {}, [], default_inputs, None
771	    try:
772	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
773	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
774	        raise ValueError(
775	            f"migration coordination ledger {realpath!r} is not valid "
776	            "UTF-8") from exc
777	    try:
778	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
779	        data = finite_loads(text)
780	    except ValueError as exc:
781	        raise ValueError(
782	            f"migration coordination ledger {realpath!r} is not valid "
783	            "JSON") from exc
784	    batches, audit, inputs = _validate_ledger(data, snapshots,
785	                                              default_inputs)
786	    if raw != _canonical_bytes(batches, audit):
787	        raise ValueError(
788	            f"migration coordination ledger {realpath!r} is not in "
789	            "canonical compact form")
790	    return batches, audit, inputs, raw

798	def _validate_receipts(receipts: object) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
799	    if receipts is None:
800	        return {}
801	    if not isinstance(receipts, dict):
802	        raise ValueError("receipts must be an object keyed by job id")
803	    checked: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
804	    for job_id, raw in receipts.items():
805	        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
806	            raise ValueError("receipt job ids must be non-empty strings")
807	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) \
808	                or set(raw.keys()) != {"step", "result", "receipt", "at"}:
809	            raise ValueError("receipt must carry step, result, receipt and "
810	                             "at")
811	        step = raw["step"]
812	        if step not in _STEPS:
813	            raise ValueError("receipt step must be copy or switch")
814	        result = raw["result"]
815	        if result not in ("succeeded", "failed"):
816	            raise ValueError("receipt result must be succeeded or failed")
817	        receipt = raw["receipt"]
818	        if not isinstance(receipt, str) or not receipt:
819	            raise ValueError("receipt text must be a non-empty string")
820	        at = raw["at"]
821	        if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
822	            raise ValueError("receipt at must be a non-boolean non-"
823	                             "negative integer")
824	        checked[job_id] = {"step": step, "result": result,
825	                           "receipt": receipt, "at": at}
826	    return checked

834	def _lease_end_for(job: dict[str, Any], at: int, lease: int) -> int:
835	    # A plan this batch starts takes one coordination-lease window,
836	    # capped at the job deadline the claim may not pass.
837	    return min(at + lease, job["deadline"])

840	def _build_members(
841	    snapshot: _Snapshot,
842	    batch_key: str,
843	    owner: str,
844	    now: int,
845	    lease: int,
846	    excluded: set[str],
847	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
848	    # Fix the membership from one complete snapshot: accepted jobs with
849	    # a trade, minus jobs another still-open batch already drives,
850	    # ordered by job id. The stage each member starts in is fixed here;
851	    # only its downstream requests advance later.
852	    members: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
853	    for job_id in sorted(snapshot.accepted):
854	        if snapshot.cleared.get(job_id) is None or job_id in excluded:
855	            continue
856	        binding = snapshot.current_binding(job_id)
857	        own_plan_key = _plan_key_for(batch_key, job_id)
858	        rooted = snapshot.rooted_plans(job_id, binding)
859	        active = next((plan for _ref, plan in rooted
860	                       if plan["state"] == "active"), None)
861	        if active is not None:
862	            # A migration round for the current binding is already in
863	            # flight: drive it with receipts, waiting or recovery.
864	            active_ref = next(ref for ref, plan in rooted if plan is active)
865	            members.append({
866	                "job_id": job_id,
867	                "plan_key": active_ref,
868	                "phase": "active",
869	                "request_key": active_ref,
870	                "lease": active["lease_end"],
871	                "error": None,
872	                "snapshot": copy.deepcopy(active),
873	            })
874	            continue
875	        terminal = next((plan for _ref, plan in reversed(rooted)
876	                         if plan["state"] in _PLAN_TERMINAL
877	                         and not any(record["plan_key"] == _ref
878	                                     for record in
879	                                     snapshot.settlements.values()
880	                                     if record["job_id"] == job_id)), None)
881	        if terminal is not None:
882	            # A terminal plan rooted at the current binding has not been
883	            # settled: enter settlement straight away; reservation and
884	            # claim are history and are never repeated.
885	            terminal_ref = next(
886	                ref for ref, plan in rooted
887	                if plan is terminal and not any(
888	                    record["job_id"] == job_id
889	                    and record["plan_key"] == ref
890	                    for record in snapshot.settlements.values()))
891	            settle_at = max(now, snapshot.terminal_moment(terminal,
892	                                                          terminal_ref))
893	            settle_key, settle_at = snapshot.settle_request(
894	                job_id, terminal_ref, settle_at,
895	                _settle_key_for(terminal_ref))
896	            members.append({
897	                "job_id": job_id,
898	                "plan_key": terminal_ref,
899	                "phase": "settling",
900	                "request_key": settle_key,
901	                "lease": terminal["lease_end"],
902	                "error": None,
903	                "snapshot": _marker("settle", plan_key=terminal_ref,
904	                                    at=settle_at),
905	            })
906	            continue
907	        unclaimed = snapshot.unclaimed_rooted_intent(job_id, binding)
908	        if unclaimed is not None:
909	            # A current-round reservation exists but has not been
910	            # claimed: claim it under the batch owner for one lease
911	            # window.
912	            _ref, intent = unclaimed
913	            lease_end = _lease_end_for(snapshot.accepted[job_id], now, lease)
914	            members.append({
915	                "job_id": job_id,
916	                "plan_key": own_plan_key,
917	                "phase": "claimed",
918	                "request_key": own_plan_key,
919	                "lease": lease_end,
920	                "error": None,
921	                "snapshot": _marker("start", owner=owner, lease_end=lease_end,
922	                                    at=now),
923	            })
924	            continue
925	        decision = snapshot.decisions.get(job_id)
926	        exec_states = {plan["state"]
927	                       for plan in snapshot.exec_plans.get(job_id, {}).values()}
928	        if decision is not None and (
929	                decision["state"] in ("succeeded", "claimed")
930	                or exec_states & {"completed", "active"}) \
931	                or now > snapshot.accepted[job_id]["deadline"]:
932	            # No current migration round and the booking itself is
933	            # finished or in flight through the baseline layers, or the
934	            # deadline has already passed so no migration is possible:
935	            # the job simply stays on its current binding.
936	            members.append({
937	                "job_id": job_id,
938	                "plan_key": None,
939	                "phase": "kept",
940	                "request_key": _stable_key(batch_key, job_id, "keep"),
941	                "lease": None,
942	                "error": None,
943	                "snapshot": binding,
944	            })
945	            continue
946	        # Otherwise the batch judges the round itself: the evaluate
947	        # call persisted below decides keep or migrate at the batch
948	        # moment, rooted at the latest completed binding.
949	        members.append({
950	            "job_id": job_id,
951	            "plan_key": own_plan_key,
952	            "phase": "evaluating",
953	            "request_key": _stable_key(batch_key, job_id, "evaluate"),
954	            "lease": None,
955	            "error": None,
956	            "snapshot": _marker("evaluate", at=now),
957	        })
958	    return members

961	def _batch_snapshot(batch: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
962	    # A fixed-order deep copy the caller can never mutate.
963	    return {
964	        "key": batch["key"],
965	        "owner": batch["owner"],
966	        "until": batch["until"],
967	        "status": batch["status"],
968	        "inputs": {name: batch["inputs"][name] for name in _INPUT_NAMES},
969	        "items": {job_id: _canonical_item(batch["items"][job_id])
970	                  for job_id in sorted(batch["items"])},
971	    }

974	def _is_business_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
975	    # The downstream interfaces' refusal vocabulary is business state
976	    # and fails just the member; locking and I/O failures surface as
977	    # OSError and abort the whole run.
978	    return not isinstance(exc, OSError) and isinstance(
979	        exc, (ValueError, KeyError, LookupError, PermissionError,
980	              TimeoutError))

988	def run(
989	    jobs: str,
990	    supply: str,
991	    signals: str,
992	    trades: str,
993	    dispatch: str,
994	    execution: str,
995	    advice: str,
996	    ledger: str,
997	    settlements: str,
998	    coordination: str,
999	    owner: str,
1000	    key: str,
1001	    now: int,
1002	    lease: int,
1003	    receipts: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
1004	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
1005	    """Coordinate one persistent batch of migrations idempotently.
1006	
1007	    The nine business ledger paths (acceptance, supply, signals,
1008	    clearing, dispatch, execution, advice, migration intent and
1009	    settlement), the coordination ledger path, ``owner`` and ``key``
1010	    must be non-empty strings and the ten paths must resolve to distinct
1011	    real locations; ``now`` must be a non-boolean non-negative integer
1012	    moment and ``lease`` a non-boolean positive integer coordination
1013	    lease (also the claim-lease window of plans this batch starts,
1014	    capped at the job deadline). ``receipts`` is an optional job-keyed
1015	    map; each receipt carries ``step`` (``copy`` or ``switch``),
1016	    ``result`` (``succeeded`` or ``failed``), a non-empty ``receipt``
1017	    string and a non-negative ``at`` moment. Any violation raises
1018	    ``ValueError`` before a business file is read.
1019	
1020	    The first call for ``key`` fixes the members from one complete
1021	    snapshot and persists them in job-id order; an empty scan still
1022	    commits a completed batch with its audit event. Each downstream
1023	    action and its parameters are durably saved before the call and the
1024	    member advances only on success, so crash re-entry replays the
1025	    original request and a completed phase is never redone. A member's
1026	    business exception saves the public exception class and fails that
1027	    member; the other members continue. The same key with a changed
1028	    ledger set raises ``ValueError`` and an active batch owned by another
1029	    caller raises ``PermissionError`` until the lease has strictly
1030	    expired.
1031	
1032	    Returns ``(batch, created)`` -- a fixed-order copy and the
1033	    first-creation flag. Missing input files or the coordination ledger
1034	    parent raise ``FileNotFoundError``; invalid arguments, receipts,
1035	    structure, ordering, references or non-canonical bytes raise
1036	    ``ValueError``; other locking or I/O failures raise ``OSError``.
1037	    """
1038	    for value in (jobs, supply, signals, trades, dispatch, execution,
1039	                  advice, ledger, settlements, coordination, owner, key):
1040	        if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
1041	            raise ValueError("the ten paths, owner and key must be "
1042	                             "non-empty strings")

1044	        raise ValueError("now must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

1046	        raise ValueError("lease must be a non-boolean positive integer")

1049	    reals = {

1052	        "signals": os.path.realpath(signals),
1053	        "trades": os.path.realpath(trades),
1054	        "dispatch": os.path.realpath(dispatch),
1055	        "execution": os.path.realpath(execution),
1056	        "advice": os.path.realpath(advice),
1057	        "ledger": os.path.realpath(ledger),
1058	        "settlements": os.path.realpath(settlements),
1059	        "coordination": os.path.realpath(coordination),
1060	    }
1061	    if len(set(reals.values())) != 10:
1062	        raise ValueError("the ten paths must be distinct real paths")
1063	    coordination_real = reals["coordination"]
1064	    paths7 = tuple(reals[name] for name in

1075	        # order. The shared locks are released around each downstream
1076	        # call (apply/start/record/recover/settle take the intent and
1077	        # settlement ledgers' own exclusive locks themselves, and
1078	        # discover the settlement ledger beside the snapshots), exactly
1079	        # as execution_sync releases its inputs before dispatching.
1080	        held: list[Any] = []

1083	            for real in sorted(set(reals[name] for name in _INPUT_NAMES)):
1084	                manager = _lock(real, shared=True)

1086	                held.append(manager)

1097	            try:

1102	                                       snapshot.input_map)
